set_plan: Set the lesson plan before any slide: the title, the objectives in pairs and the flow. Call it once, first.
set_plan.title: The lesson title.
set_plan.objectives: The objectives, each worded for the teacher and for the pupils.
set_plan.flow: One entry per slide, numbered from 1, as many as the slides you chose within the context's range.
find_picture: Find a picture for a slide: a real photo, a library picture, or a painted illustration where the subject allows. It returns the picture's src, size and aspect, and what it shows, or no picture when none fits. Several calls in one turn run at once.
find_picture.slide: The slide the picture is for.
find_picture.request: What the picture shows: the thing itself, then each thing pupils must see, each in two to four words. The slide carries any words or labels.
find_picture.kind: named for one particular real person, place, object, document, work or event; generic when any good example will do.
find_picture.period: For a historical subject, its place and time.
find_picture.aspect: Width divided by height of the box the picture will fill.
draw_diagram: Draw a diagram in the lesson's theme at the size you give. It returns the diagram's src and its labels, or the reason it could not be drawn.
draw_diagram.slide: The slide the diagram is for.
draw_diagram.request: What the diagram shows, then its labels and values, each a word, a number or a short phrase.
draw_diagram.width: Width in px of the box the diagram will fill on the 1920 × 1080 canvas.
draw_diagram.height: Height in px of that box.
render_slide: Render a slide's HTML fragment and check its geometry. It returns each violation (overflow, clipping, overlap, off canvas, text below the minimum size, a broken image) with the element and how many px, the box of every element with an id, and whether the slide can be submitted. A slide has three renders in all.
render_slide.html: The inside of the 1920 × 1080 slide: elements with inline styles or a <style> block, using the theme's var(--name) tokens. No html, head, body or script.
probe_slide: Ask yes/no questions about the latest render of a slide, answered by a vision model that sees it. One pass per render, one to five questions; yes is good.
probe_slide.questions: The probe ids to ask, those that matter for this slide.
submit_slide: Submit the slide's latest render. It is refused when that render has more violations than the slide's first render.
submit_slide.notes: Leave empty; a separate step writes the speaker notes.
finish: End the lesson once every slide is submitted. It returns any slides still missing.
